prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures an indoor workshop scene where no other people are present and the camera wearer faces a tool-lined pegboard wall roughly 0.5 to 0.8 metres in front of them, with a red toolbox below at 0.5 to 0.7 metres, an overhead wooden shelf above at 0.4 to 0.8 metres, and a receding background space on the far right in frame 1 beyond 2 metres. Across frames 1 to 3, the viewpoint turns left and tilts upward along the shelf and pegboard—showing a continuous near-to-far gradient from about 0.4 metres on the right to 1.5 metres at the upper-left corner in frame 3—before turning back right in frames 4 and 5 as the wearer's right arm enters within 0.2 to 0.5 metres. Everything on the lower pegboard, red toolbox, and overhead shelf lip lies within the camera wearer's arm's reach (under 0.7 metres), and in frame 5 the bright white foreground arm clearly occludes the right side of the pegboard and shelf behind it. Compared to the motion-blurred RGB strip, the depth map more clearly separates the overhanging shelf plane from the recessed cavity underneath it and highlights the protruding 3D relief of the hanging mallets and tools in frame 4. However, the depth map is unreliable around small thin tools in frames 1 and 2 where fine contours merge into the flat pegboard plane, and on the foreground arm in frame 5 where depth saturates to uniform white.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is almost entirely blank across the scene, detecting none of the workshop structures, hanging tools, overhead shelving, or the red toolbox, and showing no other people facing or looking toward the camera wearer. In frame 5, a pink 'person' mask identifies the camera wearer's raised right arm and hand extending diagonally from the bottom-right corner to the top-right shelf edge at roughly 0.2 to 0.5 metres from the camera, partially out of view at the frame borders and occluding the right edge of the pegboard. Across the five frames, this map registers no objects during the leftward pan in frames 1 and 2, places a narrow mask at the bottom-right boundary of frame 3, misses the wearer's hand reaching for the earmuffs at the bottom-right of frame 4, and then segments the raised arm in frame 5. The mask in frame 5 cleanly isolates the silhouette of the wearer's foreground limb from the motion-blurred background wall, which is harder to trace precisely in the RGB image. However, the segmentation map is largely unreliable here: it completely misses the wearer's visible hand in frame 4, falsely labels a hanging hammer on the right edge of frame 3 (about 0.4 metres away) as a 'person', and produces two small spurious 'person' fragments over the red toolbox and upper-right background in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains no yellow body skeletons across any of the five frames because no other people are present in the room to face or look toward the camera wearer, leaving only magenta hand keypoints for the camera wearer's own right hand in frames 4 and 5. In frames 1 through 3, as the camera turns left and tilts upward toward the overhead shelf and pegboard, the pose map remains completely black because the wearer's hands are out of view below the frame. In frame 4, a magenta hand skeleton appears at the bottom-right corner about 0.4 to 0.5 metres in front of the camera wearer, positioned directly on the hanging earmuffs to the right of the hammers and below the shelf. In frame 5, as the camera tilts slightly down and right, the magenta hand skeleton shifts to the top-right edge at roughly 0.4 to 0.5 metres away, grasping the upper shelf above the pegboard while its fingertips are partly clipped by the top image boundary. This map reveals exact finger joint articulations during contact with the earmuffs in frame 4 and the shelf in frame 5 that are obscured by heavy motion blur in the RGB frames, though it is incomplete in frame 5 where the missing arm skeleton leaves the raised forearm unrepresented and upper finger joints are cut off at the frame edge.
